audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's demand to argue his case before God, rebuke of friends as whitewashers/false healers, legal-risk language, and plea for God to remove terror and disclose charges.

verses.restored: Look, my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard and understood it.

familiar.text: Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, mine ear hath heard and understood it.

modern.text: “Indeed, my eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood.

original.text: הֶן כֹּ֭ל רָאֲתָ֣ה עֵינִ֑י שָֽׁמְעָ֥ה אָ֝זְנִ֗י וַתָּ֥בֶן לָֽהּ

verses.restored: What you know, I also know; I do not fall below you.

familiar.text: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.

modern.text: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.

original.text: כְּֽ֭דַעְתְּכֶם יָדַ֣עְתִּי גַם אָ֑נִי לֹא נֹפֵ֖ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּֽם

verses.restored: But I would speak to Shaddai, and I desire to argue with the Divine.

familiar.text: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.

modern.text: Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.

original.text: אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶל שַׁדַּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְהוֹכֵ֖חַ אֶל אֵ֣ל אֶחְפָּֽץ

verses.restored: But you are smearers of falsehood; all of you are worthless healers.

familiar.text: But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.

modern.text: You, however, smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.

original.text: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם אַתֶּ֥ם טֹֽפְלֵי שָׁ֑קֶר רֹפְאֵ֖י אֱלִ֣ל כֻּלְּכֶֽם

verses.restored: If only you would be completely silent; that would become your wisdom.

familiar.text: O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom.

modern.text: If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!

original.text: מִֽי יִ֭תֵּן הַחֲרֵ֣שׁ תַּחֲרִישׁ֑וּן וּתְהִ֖י לָכֶ֣ם לְחָכְמָֽה

verses.restored: Please hear my argument, and listen to the pleadings of my lips.

familiar.text: Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.

modern.text: Hear now my argument, and listen to the plea of my lips.

original.text: שִׁמְעוּ נָ֥א תוֹכַחְתִּ֑י וְרִב֖וֹת שְׂפָתַ֣י הַקְשִֽׁיבוּ

verses.restored: Will you speak injustice for the Divine, and speak deceit for him?

familiar.text: Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?

modern.text: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?

original.text: הַ֭לְאֵל תְּדַבְּר֣וּ עַוְלָ֑ה וְ֝ל֗וֹ תְּֽדַבְּר֥וּ רְמִיָּֽה

verses.restored: Will you lift his face? Will you contend for the Divine?

familiar.text: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?

modern.text: Would you show Him partiality or argue in His defense?

original.text: הֲפָנָ֥יו תִּשָּׂא֑וּן אִם לָאֵ֥ל תְּרִיבֽוּן

verses.restored: Will it be good when he searches you out? Or can you deceive him as one deceives a mortal?

familiar.text: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye so mock him?

modern.text: Would it be well when He examined you? Could you deceive Him like a man?

original.text: הֲ֭טוֹב כִּֽי יַחְקֹ֣ר אֶתְכֶ֑ם אִם כְּהָתֵ֥ל בֶּ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ תְּהָתֵ֥לּוּ בֽוֹ

verses.restored: He will surely rebuke you if in secret you lift faces.

familiar.text: He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons.

modern.text: Surely He would rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.

original.text: הוֹכֵ֣חַ יוֹכִ֣יחַ אֶתְכֶ֑ם אִם בַּ֝סֵּ֗תֶר פָּנִ֥ים תִּשָּׂאֽוּן

verses.restored: Will not his majesty terrify you, and his dread fall upon you?

familiar.text: Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you?

modern.text: Would His majesty not terrify you? Would the dread of Him not fall upon you?

original.text: הֲלֹ֣א שְׂ֭אֵתוֹ תְּבַעֵ֣ת אֶתְכֶ֑ם וּ֝פַחְדּ֗וֹ יִפֹּ֥ל עֲלֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ash; your defenses are defenses of clay.

familiar.text: Your remembrances are like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.

modern.text: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.

original.text: זִֽ֭כְרֹנֵיכֶם מִשְׁלֵי אֵ֑פֶר לְגַבֵּי חֹ֝֗מֶר גַּבֵּיכֶֽם

verses.restored: Be silent from me, and I myself will speak; let whatever may pass over me pass.

familiar.text: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what will.

modern.text: Be silent, and I will speak. Then let come to me what may.

original.text: הַחֲרִ֣ישׁוּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי וַאֲדַבְּרָה אָ֑נִי וְיַעֲבֹ֖ר עָלַ֣י מָֽה

verses.restored: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my palm?

familiar.text: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in mine hand?

modern.text: Why do I put myself at risk and take my life in my own hands?

original.text: עַל מָ֤ה אֶשָּׂ֣א בְשָׂרִ֣י בְשִׁנָּ֑י וְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י אָשִׂ֥ים בְּכַפִּֽי

verses.restored: Though he slay me, I will wait/hope for him; yet I will argue my ways to his face.

familiar.text: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him.

modern.text: Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.

original.text: הֵ֣ן יִ֭קְטְלֵנִי לא אֲיַחֵ֑ל אַךְ דְּ֝רָכַ֗י אֶל פָּנָ֥יו אוֹכִֽיחַ

verses.restored: This also will be my salvation, for a godless person cannot come before him.

familiar.text: He also shall be my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.

modern.text: Moreover, this will be my salvation, for no godless man can appear before Him.

original.text: גַּם הוּא לִ֥י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה כִּי לֹ֥א לְ֝פָנָ֗יו חָנֵ֥ף יָבֽוֹא

verses.restored: Hear carefully my word, and let my declaration be in your ears.

familiar.text: Hear diligently my speech, and my declaration with your ears.

modern.text: Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears.

original.text: שִׁמְע֣וּ שָׁ֭מוֹעַ מִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝אַֽחֲוָתִ֗י בְּאָזְנֵיכֶֽם

verses.restored: Look now, I have arranged my case; I know that I myself am right.

familiar.text: Behold now, I have ordered my cause; I know that I shall be justified.

modern.text: Behold, now that I have prepared my case, I know that I will be vindicated.

original.text: הִנֵּה נָ֭א עָרַ֣כְתִּי מִשְׁפָּ֑ט יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י אֶצְדָּֽק

verses.restored: Who is he who will contend with me? For then I would be silent and expire.

familiar.text: Who is he that will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.

modern.text: Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.

original.text: מִי ה֭וּא יָרִ֣יב עִמָּדִ֑י כִּֽי עַתָּ֖ה אַחֲרִ֣ישׁ וְאֶגְוָֽע

verses.restored: Only two things do not do to me; then I will not hide myself from your face:

familiar.text: Only do not two things unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.

modern.text: Only grant these two things to me, so that I need not hide from You:

original.text: אַךְ שְׁ֭תַּיִם אַל תַּ֣עַשׂ עִמָּדִ֑י אָ֥ז מִ֝פָּנֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א אֶסָּתֵֽר

verses.restored: Remove your hand far from me, and let your terror not frighten me.

familiar.text: Withdraw thine hand far from me: and let not thy dread make me afraid.

modern.text: Withdraw Your hand from me, and do not let Your terror frighten me.

original.text: כַּ֭פְּךָ מֵעָלַ֣י הַרְחַ֑ק וְ֝אֵ֥מָתְךָ֗ אַֽל תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי

verses.restored: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you reply to me.

familiar.text: Then call thou, and I will answer: or let me speak, and answer thou me.

modern.text: Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.

original.text: וּ֭קְרָא וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה אֽוֹ אֲ֝דַבֵּ֗ר וַהֲשִׁיבֵֽנִי

verses.restored: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my transgression and my sin.

familiar.text: How many are mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.

modern.text: How many are my iniquities and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and sin.

original.text: כַּמָּ֣ה לִ֭י עֲוֺנ֣וֹת וְחַטָּא֑וֹת פִּֽשְׁעִ֥י וְ֝חַטָּאתִ֗י הֹדִיעֵֽנִי

verses.restored: Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?

familiar.text: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy?

modern.text: Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?

original.text: לָֽמָּה פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר וְתַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Will you terrify a driven leaf and pursue dry stubble?

familiar.text: Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?

modern.text: Would You frighten a windblown leaf? Would You chase after dry chaff?

original.text: הֶעָלֶ֣ה נִדָּ֣ף תַּעֲר֑וֹץ וְאֶת קַ֖שׁ יָבֵ֣שׁ תִּרְדֹּֽף

verses.restored: For you write bitter things against me and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.

familiar.text: For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth.

modern.text: For You record bitter accusations against me and bequeath to me the iniquities of my youth.

original.text: כִּֽי תִכְתֹּ֣ב עָלַ֣י מְרֹר֑וֹת וְ֝תוֹרִישֵׁ֗נִי עֲוֺנ֥וֹת נְעוּרָֽי

verses.restored: You put my feet in the stocks, watch all my paths, and trace the soles of my feet.

familiar.text: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet.

modern.text: You put my feet in the stocks and stand watch over all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.

original.text: וְתָ֘שֵׂ֤ם בַּסַּ֨ד רַגְלַ֗י וְתִשְׁמ֥וֹר כָּל אָרְחוֹתָ֑י עַל שָׁרְשֵׁ֥י רַ֝גְלַ֗י תִּתְחַקֶּֽה

verses.restored: And he wears away like rot, like a garment eaten by moths.

familiar.text: And he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment that is moth eaten.

modern.text: So man wastes away like something rotten, like a moth-eaten garment.

original.text: וְ֭הוּא כְּרָקָ֣ב יִבְלֶ֑ה כְּ֝בֶ֗גֶד אֲכָ֣לוֹ עָֽשׁ
